title: Orsen and the Contact
premise: Isandro Okonkwo, a sleep-wrecked private security contractor haunted by a botched protection job she can't fully remember, is approached by a stranger who insists Isandro once saved her life — a favor Isandro has no memory of. The stranger's payment is information: her current client, a shadowy logistics firm, is using Isandro's security detail as cover for a black-site operation, and the defector she's been hired to extract is bait designed to flush out the firm's enemies — including the stranger. As Isandro digs into her own missing memories and the firm closes in, she must decide whether the defector is victim or trap, racing to get him onto a dawn extraction flight while exposing the operation that stole her nights. In the end, Isandro chooses to burn her contract, spring the defector through the firm's own security perimeter, and confront the handler who engineered both the incident and her amnesia — walking away with the truth, the defector alive, and no one left to trust but herself.
about_author: Cyrus Halloran is a former maritime insurance investigator who spent a decade documenting how quietly corporations make people disappear from their own lives. He writes thrillers from a houseboat in Rotterdam, where he claims the best plot ideas arrive at 3 a.m.

chapters.title: The Hours Between
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A sleepless night on a routine protection detail in Rotterdam establishes her insomnia, her meticulous professionalism, and the gap in her memory she calls 'the incident.' Emotional beat: brittle control masking dread.

chapters.title: Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Isandro meets her new employer, Meridian Logistics, whose fixer offers triple rate for a discreet extraction job — no questions, no paper trail. Her partner Teo urges refusal; debt says otherwise. Beat: unease priced into every decision.

chapters.title: A Favor Returned
chapters.summary: A woman named Vera Kessler corners Isandro outside a café, thanking her for saving her life in Lisbon — an event Isandro cannot recall at all. Vera leaves a keycard and a warning: check your own logs. Beat: vertigo of a past that doesn't fit.

chapters.title: Logs That Lie
chapters.summary: Isandro audits her company's records and finds six days of her Lisbon deployment scrubbed clean, her own signature forged on the redactions. POV alternates with a brief Meridian handler scene showing surveillance on her. Beat: paranoia becomes evidence.

chapters.title: The Defector File
chapters.summary: Isandro reviews the target: Dr. Emil Rask, a biometric-data scientist fleeing Meridian's black program. His file contains a photo of Isandro taken in Lisbon — before she ever took this contract. Beat: the job was always about her.

chapters.title: Teo's Doubts
chapters.summary: Teo confronts Isandro about Meridian's payment structure, which mirrors the setup that got their old team burned. Flashback fragments surface: gunfire, a stairwell, someone screaming her name. Beat: loyalty strained by pattern recognition.

chapters.title: Vera's Version
chapters.summary: Vera explains Lisbon: Meridian ran an off-book interrogation site; Isandro's team stumbled into it; Vera was the prisoner Isandro let slip away before her own memory was chemically wiped. Beat: grief for a self she can't access.

chapters.title: Chemistry of Forgetting
chapters.summary: Isandro tracks the compound used on her through a disgraced pharmacologist, learning the wipe is imperfect — memories return under specific sensory triggers. Beat: hope weaponized; recovery will hurt.

chapters.title: First Trigger
chapters.summary: Rain on a stairwell triggers a full flashback: Isandro did free Vera, and her team leader Dario sold the team out to cover it. Two colleagues died. Beat: rage with nowhere safe to aim it.

chapters.title: Rask Makes Contact
chapters.summary: The defector himself reaches out through a dead drop, insisting he requested Isandro specifically — because her name appears in Meridian's experiment ledgers as Subject Nine. Beat: from contractor to specimen.

chapters.title: Subject Nine
chapters.summary: Isandro decodes ledger entries: Meridian tests memory erasure on disposable contractors, then redeploys them as deniable assets. She realizes her insomnia may be the drug fighting her brain. Beat: body as crime scene.

chapters.title: The Handler Smiles
chapters.summary: Meridian's handler, Calloway, warmly reassures Isandro over dinner, subtly testing what she remembers. She performs ignorance flawlessly. Beat: a duel fought entirely in subtext.

chapters.title: Extraction Plan Alpha
chapters.summary: Isandro drafts the legitimate plan: extract Rask via dawn cargo flight from Rotterdam-The Hague. She builds a second, secret plan layered inside it. Beat: competence as armor.

chapters.title: Bait Theory
chapters.summary: Vera argues Rask is bait — his defection too easy, his route too clean, designed to draw out Meridian's enemies. Isandro must weigh the man against the trap. Beat: trust as calculated risk.

chapters.title: Rask's Confession
chapters.summary: Meeting Rask in person, Isandro hears his confession: he built the erasure protocol, and his defection is partly penance, partly escape. He confirms Subject Nine exists — and that she volunteered once, to forget something worse. Beat: sympathy curdled by doubt.

chapters.title: What She Chose to Lose
chapters.summary: Under guided recall, Isandro recovers the buried core: in Lisbon she discovered Meridian's program held children of test subjects, and she signed the wipe to protect herself from being made to talk. Beat: shame, the heaviest theme.

chapters.title: Calloway Tightens
chapters.summary: Meridian moves the extraction up twelve hours and adds its own shooters to Isandro's team — men she recognizes from Lisbon. Beat: the walls rearranging around her.

chapters.title: Teo Learns Everything
chapters.summary: Isandro tells Teo the whole truth, gambling their partnership. He reveals he's been skimming Meridian intel for months out of suspicion. Beat: two liars choosing honesty.

chapters.title: The Keycard Opens
chapters.summary: Vera's keycard opens a Meridian archive node where Isandro finds the children's transfer manifests — still active routes. Beat: personal stakes become moral ones.

chapters.title: Complications at Dawn Minus Two
chapters.summary: The flight slot changes again; Rask's safehouse is compromised; a Meridian kill team deploys. Isandro improvises a new route through the port. Beat: adrenaline with cold clarity.

chapters.title: Port of Shadows
chapters.summary: Nighttime chase through container yards; Isandro extracts Rask seconds ahead of the kill team, using her own security credentials against Meridian's perimeter. Beat: the hunted turning hunter.

chapters.title: Betrayal Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Reviewing the leak, Isandro deduces only Teo could have known the safehouse — or Vera. Both deny it; evidence points at each. Beat: trust fracturing under pressure.

chapters.title: Vera's Real Name
chapters.summary: Isandro discovers 'Vera Kessler' is an alias of a Meridian internal-affairs officer hunting the program from inside — her gratitude may be genuine, her methods not. Beat: ally, asset, or angler?

chapters.title: Interrogation of Memory
chapters.summary: Using the pharmacologist's trigger method deliberately, Isandro reconstructs the full Lisbon night, including Dario's face at the stairwell door. Dario now runs Meridian's field division. Beat: the ghost gets a name and a rank.

chapters.title: Dario Calls
chapters.summary: Dario contacts Isandro directly: come back, hand over Rask, and he'll restore her records and erase her debts — the same deal she took once before. Beat: temptation wearing a familiar voice.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Isandro declines and burns her Meridian credentials, going dark with Rask and Teo. Meridian flags them all. Beat: liberation that feels like falling.

chapters.title: The Children's Route
chapters.summary: The trio plans a double strike: get Rask on the dawn flight AND pass the children's manifests to a journalist and Europol contact. Beat: purpose replacing survival.

chapters.title: Safehouse Siege
chapters.summary: Meridian's shooters find them; a brutal close-quarters defense leaves Teo wounded and their location burned. Beat: cost made physical.

chapters.title: Field Medicine and Hard Choices
chapters.summary: While treating Teo, Isandro must choose between splitting up to guarantee the flight or staying together and missing it. Rask volunteers to go alone — possibly to surrender. Beat: sacrifice offered, refused.

chapters.title: Calloway's Trap Springs
chapters.summary: At the airport perimeter, Calloway reveals the whole extraction was monitored; he offers Isandro Rask's life for her return as an asset. Beat: power's corruption offered as employment.

chapters.title: Countermove
chapters.summary: Isandro springs her hidden second plan: the 'dawn flight' Calloway watched was a decoy charter; the real flight leaves from a military strip via a favor Teo cashed long ago. Beat: patience paying off.

chapters.title: Confrontation on the Tarmac
chapters.summary: Dario intercepts them anyway. Isandro faces the man who sold her team, and instead of killing him, she records his confession to the program as sirens approach. Beat: justice chosen over vengeance.

chapters.title: Flight at First Light
chapters.summary: Rask boards as the sun rises; Europol takes custody arrangements mid-taxi. Isandro watches the plane climb — the deadline met, barely. Beat: exhale after held breath.

chapters.title: Aftermath and Arrests
chapters.summary: Manifests land with journalist Anouk de Vries; arrests begin across three countries. Calloway vanishes, leaving a message: the program has owners above him. Beat: victory with loose threads.

chapters.title: Teo's Decision
chapters.summary: Recovering, Teo chooses to leave contracting altogether; he and Isandro part as equals, honestly. Beat: friendship surviving truth.

chapters.title: Vera Settles Accounts
chapters.summary: Vera, exposed but protected by her whistleblower status, gives Isandro her complete Lisbon file — including proof Isandro shielded two children before wiping herself. Beat: mercy toward one's past self.

chapters.title: Sleep Returns
chapters.summary: For the first time since Lisbon, Isandro sleeps through the night — then wakes and chooses to remember everything on purpose, writing her own account. Beat: memory reclaimed as authorship.

chapters.title: The Owners Above
chapters.summary: Anouk's reporting forces inquiries, but Isandro identifies a Meridian board figure connected to the children's routes still untouched. Beat: the war isn't over, just relocated.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Isandro rebuilds — small office, honest clients, Teo consulting occasionally — and turns down a lucrative offer that rhymes too much with Meridian. Beat: belonging chosen, not bought.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Months later, one of the rescued children, grown, contacts Isandro to say thank you — the favor returned that finally happened. Isandro answers the phone as dawn breaks. Beat: closure earned, future open.
